# Polska: Poland as a strategy map built from real data: full text

Every atlas page of https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/ as compact markdown. Generated 2026-11-27. Each figure gives its date and publisher.

## Poland in numbers

Poland had 37,242,958 residents on 30 June 2026. Between 2015 and 2025 the population fell by 2.9%.

The country has 16 voivodeships, 2,479 gminas, 380 powiats and 1,026 towns.

Its GDP was 3.92 trillion zł in 2025. Mazowieckie, around Warszawa, is the largest voivodeship by population and produced 24.0% of the national GDP in 2024.

Each voivodeship and each town of 20,000 or more people has its own page below, with its figures and their sources.

### National figures

- Population: 37,242,958 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -2.9% (from 38,434,668) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 3.92 trillion zł (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- GDP per resident: 105,131 zł (2025 GDP, 2026 residents; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 9,178 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 5.8% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 15,125,030 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,328 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- UNESCO World Heritage properties: 18 (2026; UNESCO World Heritage Centre (data.unesco.org); Narodowy Instytut Dziedzictwa (dane.gov.pl))
- National parks: 23 (2024; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); Wikidata)
- Visits to national parks: 16,390,532 (2024; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); Wikidata)

## Dolnośląskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/dolnoslaskie/

Dolnośląskie has the 2nd highest average gross wage of the 16 voivodeships: 9,208 zł a month in May 2026.

Its capital is Wrocław.

It has 93 towns; 16 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 2,851,302 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -1.6% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 303 billion zł (8.3% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 9,208 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 5.5% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 1,117,241 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,593 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 82.1 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 75.2 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 4.1 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 11.4 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 41% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Wrocław](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wroclaw/): 672,579 residents
- [Wałbrzych](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/walbrzych/): 96,904 residents
- [Legnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/legnica/): 89,484 residents
- [Jelenia Góra](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/jelenia-gora/): 73,029 residents
- [Lubin](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/lubin/): 65,607 residents
- [Głogów](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/glogow/): 60,287 residents
- [Świdnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/swidnica/): 51,073 residents
- [Bolesławiec](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/boleslawiec/): 36,504 residents
- [Oleśnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/olesnica/): 34,498 residents
- [Oława](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/olawa/): 32,872 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Churches of Peace in Jawor and Świdnica: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2001
- Centennial Hall in Wrocław: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2006
- Karkonoski Park Narodowy: National park, 2,400,000 visits in 2024
- Park Narodowy Gór Stołowych: National park, 1,296,300 visits in 2024
- Uniwersytet Wrocławski: University, 21,426 students on 31 December 2025

### Energy and resources

- Elektrownia Turów: Lignite power plant, 1,995 MW
- Elektrociepłownia Wrocław: Hard-coal power plant, 260 MW
- Elektrociepłownia Czechnica 2: Gas power plant, 179 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna PV Kotla: Solar power plant, 130 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna PV Miłkowice: Solar power plant, 113 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna Proszówek: Solar power plant, 55 MW
- KWB Turów: Lignite mine, 7.0 Mt lignite (2025)
- Głogów Głęboki-Przemysłowy (shaft GG-1): Copper mine
- ZG Lubin: Copper mine
- ZG Polkowice-Sieroszowice: Copper mine
- ZG Rudna: Copper mine
- Huta Miedzi Cedynia: Copper smelter

## Kujawsko-Pomorskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/kujawsko-pomorskie/

Kujawsko-Pomorskie has the least tree cover of the 16 voivodeships: 31% of its land.

The voivode sits in Bydgoszcz and the regional assembly (sejmik) in Toruń.

It has 56 towns; 7 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 1,965,028 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -5.5% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 154 billion zł (4.2% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,206 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 7.7% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 660,444 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 3,845 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 81.7 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 74.7 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 1.8 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 3.7 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 31% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Bydgoszcz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/bydgoszcz/): 319,528 residents
- [Toruń](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/torun/): 192,159 residents
- [Włocławek](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wloclawek/): 97,435 residents
- [Grudziądz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/grudziadz/): 86,425 residents
- [Inowrocław](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/inowroclaw/): 65,329 residents
- [Brodnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/brodnica/): 27,577 residents
- [Świecie](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/swiecie/): 24,385 residents
- Chełmno: 17,372 residents
- Nakło nad Notecią: 16,553 residents
- Rypin: 15,047 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Medieval Town of Toruń: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997

### Energy and resources

- Budowa bloku gazowo-parowego CCGT w Grudziądzu: Gas power plant, 560 MW (under_construction)
- Elektrociepłownia Gazowo-Parowa Anwil Włocławek: Gas power plant, 463 MW
- PGE Energia Ciepła S.A. Oddział Elektrociepłownia w Bydgoszczy: Hard-coal power plant, 187 MW

- Life expectancy at birth, women: 82.0 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 74.2 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 1.0 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 6.7 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 60% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

## Łódzkie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/lodzkie/

Women in Łódzkie have the shortest life expectancy of the 16 voivodeships: 81.4 years at birth in 2025.

Its capital is Łódź.

It has 60 towns; 13 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 2,319,537 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -6.6% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 220 billion zł (6.0% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,424 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 6.4% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 878,997 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,337 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 81.4 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 73.9 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 2.0 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 9.0 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))

## Małopolskie

## Śląskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/slaskie/

Śląskie is the 2nd most populous voivodeship, with 4,246,702 residents on 30 June 2026.

Its capital is Katowice.

It has 75 towns; 36 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 4,246,702 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -6.8% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 420 billion zł (11.5% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,753 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 4.8% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 1,584,161 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,867 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 81.8 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 74.9 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 3.2 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 8.4 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 53% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Katowice](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/katowice/): 276,563 residents
- [Częstochowa](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/czestochowa/): 200,295 residents
- [Sosnowiec](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/sosnowiec/): 181,983 residents
- [Gliwice](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/gliwice/): 166,205 residents
- [Bielsko-Biała](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/bielsko-biala/): 162,517 residents
- [Zabrze](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/zabrze/): 150,108 residents
- [Bytom](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/bytom/): 143,853 residents
- [Rybnik](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/rybnik/): 128,360 residents
- [Ruda Śląska](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/ruda-slaska/): 126,922 residents
- [Tychy](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/tychy/): 119,592 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Tarnowskie Góry Lead-Silver-Zinc Mine and its Underground Water Management System: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2017

### Energy and resources

- Elektrownia Jaworzno III: Hard-coal power plant, 2,255 MW
- TAURON Wytwarzanie S. A. Oddział Elektrownia Łaziska w Łaziskach Górnych: Hard-coal power plant, 905 MW
- PGE Energia Ciepła Oddział w Rybniku: Hard-coal power plant, 900 MW

- Elektrownia Łagisza: Hard-coal power plant, 460 MW
- KWK Bobrek: Hard-coal mine (closed)
- KWK Bolesław Śmiały: Hard-coal mine, 1.8 Mt raw coal (2025)
- KWK Borynia-Zofiówka: Hard-coal mine, 7.9 Mt raw coal (2025)
- KWK Budryk: Hard-coal mine, 3.9 Mt raw coal (2025)
- KWK Knurów-Szczygłowice: Hard-coal mine, 6.3 Mt raw coal (2025)

## Świętokrzyskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/swietokrzyskie/

Świętokrzyskie lost 8.7% of its residents between 2015 and 2025, the steepest fall of the 16 voivodeships.

Its capital is Kielce.

It has 51 towns; 5 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 1,141,621 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -8.7% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 84.6 billion zł (2.3% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,105 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 8.4% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 373,349 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 3,483 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 83.1 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 75.1 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 2.1 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 5.8 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 45% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Kielce](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/kielce/): 177,980 residents
- [Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/ostrowiec-swietokrzyski/): 59,825 residents
- [Starachowice](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/starachowice/): 43,006 residents
- [Skarżysko-Kamienna](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/skarzysko-kamienna/): 39,772 residents
- [Sandomierz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/sandomierz/): 20,589 residents
- Końskie: 16,770 residents
- Busko-Zdrój: 13,763 residents
- Jędrzejów: 13,585 residents
- Staszów: 13,108 residents
- Pińczów: 9,368 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Krzemionki Prehistoric Striped Flint Mining Region: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2019

### Energy and resources

- Elektrownia Połaniec: Hard-coal power plant, 1,882 MW

### Town pages in Świętokrzyskie

## Wielkopolskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wielkopolskie/

Wielkopolskie has the lowest registered unemployment of the 16 voivodeships: 3.8% in October 2026.

Its capital is Poznań.

It has 120 towns; 17 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 3,465,649 (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -0.1% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 361 billion zł (9.8% of Poland) (2024; Statistics Poland (GUS), Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,271 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 3.8% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 1,699,670 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,183 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 82.2 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 75.5 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 3.0 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 10.5 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 33% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

## Warszawa

Warszawa, Mazowieckie. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/warszawa/

Warszawa is the capital and the largest city of Poland, with 1,866,929 residents on 30 June 2026.

Warszawa is the capital of Poland and a city with powiat rights in Mazowieckie voivodeship. It is the capital of Mazowieckie.

### Figures

- Population: 1,866,929 (30 June 2026; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: +7.0% (from 1,744,351) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 42.4 years (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 20.2% (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage: 12,059 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 1.6% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 8,040 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- University students per 1,000 residents: 140 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working in the city: 1,983,029 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

City type: Capital city. Capital of Poland.

Jobs by employer seat on 31 December 2025, against the share of each kind of work in Poland.

- Commercial hub district (Trade, Finance, Real estate, Business services): 637,049 workers, 1.5 times the national share; Finance alone 4.0 times
- Campus district (IT & telecoms, Science & engineering, Schools & universities): 522,772 workers, 1.5 times the national share; IT & telecoms alone 2.6 times
- Theater square district (Arts, sport & recreation): 31,746 workers, 1.4 times the national share

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 68.2% of valid votes in Warszawa and Karol Nawrocki 31.8%. Turnout was 83.2%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

### Air quality

PM2.5 averaged 15.6 µg/m³ in 2025 at the GIOŚ station Warszawa, al. Niepodległości (3 km).

The median of the 154 towns of 20,000+ with a station within 25 km was 16.4 µg/m³.

### Metro area and places nearby

Warszawa belongs to the Warszawa metro area, 3,539,344 residents in 97 gminas.

- Uniwersytet Warszawski: University, 39,852 students on 31 December 2025, in the town
- Politechnika Warszawska: University, 20,953 students on 31 December 2025, in the town
- Varso Tower: Tallest building in Poland: 310 m (2022), in the town
- Historic Centre of Warsaw: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1980, 2 km away
- Warszawa-Chopin: Busiest airport by passengers: 24,079,757 passengers (2025), 8 km away

Katowice has 187 university students per 1,000 residents, the 4th highest share of the 84 towns of 20,000+ with a university.

Katowice is a city with powiat rights in Śląskie voivodeship. It is the capital of Śląskie.

### Figures

- Population: 276,563 (30 June 2026; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: -7.5% (from 299,910) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 45.2 years (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 24.3% (30 June 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage: 10,112 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 1.9% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 6,272 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- University students per 1,000 residents: 187 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working in the city: 255,529 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

City type: Coal town. KWK Staszic-Wujek.

Jobs by employer seat on 31 December 2025, against the share of each kind of work in Poland.

- Mining (Industrial zone district): 36,115 workers, 17.3 times the national share
- Government plaza district (Public administration & defence): 32,984 workers, 1.8 times the national share
- Theater square district (Arts, sport & recreation): 3,820 workers, 1.3 times the national share

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 63.1% of valid votes in Katowice and Karol Nawrocki 36.9%. Turnout was 74.8%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

### Air quality

PM2.5 averaged 18.1 µg/m³ in 2025 at the GIOŚ station Katowice, ul. Dudy-Gracza (6 km).

The median of the 154 towns of 20,000+ with a station within 25 km was 16.4 µg/m³.

### Metro area and places nearby

Katowice belongs to the Górnośląsko-Zagłębiowska metro area (PL010F, PL055F, PL061F, PL070F), 2,013,732 residents in 39 gminas.

- Tarnowskie Góry Lead-Silver-Zinc Mine and its Underground Water Management System: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2017, 24 km away
- Auschwitz Birkenau German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp (1940-1945): Memorial and museum, UNESCO World Heritage since 1979, 29 km away

These figures describe the jobs in powiat zambrowski, by employer seat, on 31 December 2025.

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 34.3% of valid votes in Zambrów and Karol Nawrocki 65.7%. Turnout was 64.5%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Prawo i Sprawiedliwość.
